topics.topic: Startup cleanup of unreferenced content-addressed value bytes
questions: Which startup operation removes content-addressed value bytes that no record names?
Does `store.open_store` remove unreferenced content-addressed value bytes at startup, and if not, which operation does?
Must open_store remove unreferenced content-addressed value bytes at startup, and does a failure to remove them stop startup?

quotes:
On start, temporary files,
   value bytes no record names (left by a failed call, so only trial fixtures
   and named values outlive a run, K-10; owner, 2026-10-07) and
   the spool directories of runs that ended and do not keep their spool (A14) are
   removed; nothing else is.

The store's own temporary files — those it writes before a rename (A18 rule 4)
— are removed, and nothing else is; the database schema, the
content-addressed area and the spool area are created inside the data
directory when absent.
judgement.why: A18 requires startup removal of unnamed value bytes, while State 5 says open_store removes only temporary files and nothing else.

topics.topic: Allowed api_base_url syntax, normalization, joining, and loopback classification
questions: What URL grammar and joining rules apply to base URLs containing a path, multiple trailing slashes, user information, an IPv6 literal, percent escapes, a query or a fragment, and what exactly counts as a loopback host?

Are user information, query, fragment and an existing base path allowed in `api_base_url`; how many trailing slashes are removed; and how are these components represented in the request URL, Host header and approval digest?

quotes:
the installation selects no instance for the service or that
   instance has no `api_base_url` — one that is not an absolute `http` or
   `https` URL with a host counts as none — or names one required header
   twice, or names one the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7) other than `host`, which an
   instance may set instead of the kernel (A10 rule 7), names compared without
   regard to case — at send time both are A09 rule 6's `required_header_repeated`
   —, or has a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character — at send time `required_header_invalid`;

The
   URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared
   path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..`
   segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host; a `{` or `}` appears only in a
   placeholder, which is one whole segment `{name}` whose name is not empty and
   contains no `{`, `}` or `/`, and no name is a placeholder twice; a path that
   does not is not invocable (A08 rule 3). Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they
   stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.

Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
   The host judged here, the one connected to, and for `https` the server name
   sent and verified, are always those of `api_base_url`; a required `Host`
   header (A10 rule 7) changes only the header sent.

`host` — the authority of `api_base_url` exactly as the manifest writes it,
   not normalized (A09 rule 1), unless the instance's required headers name
   `host`, in which case that required header is sent instead, its value
   verbatim, and is the only `host` —, `accept-encoding: identity` (A09 rule 3),
judgement.divergence: One implementer rejects base URLs containing user information, an existing path, query, fragment, unusual percent escapes, or noncanonical IPv6 and recognizes loopback only from IP literals; another accepts them, removes a different number of trailing slashes, concatenates components differently, or resolves names for loopback. The called service observes a different target URL or rejection, and the owner observes a different Host header and approval request digest.
judgement.why: The texts constrain an absolute HTTP(S) URL and simple concatenation but do not close the accepted URL grammar, slash handling, component interaction, or loopback classification.
judgement.deferred_to: the states whose texts it quotes

topics.topic: Applicable startup capability checks and deterministic failure ordering
questions: Which A08 checks are applied when this startup operation has no operation name or proposed ports, and in what order are failures among several capabilities reported?
Which exact A08 rule 5 checks are checks of the service record itself during startup when check_installed_instances has no operation name or proposed ports?

judgement.why: This is the same startup manifest-validation scope and ordering question already decided by P1, and the relevant State 5 passages were not changed.

precedent.topic: Scope of service-manifest validation performed during startup
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.

topics.topic: Deterministic ordering of FlowConstants targeting the same node and port
questions: How are different constants targeting the same node and port ordered before hashing the order-free constants list?
How are multiple constants targeting the same node and port ordered before the proof rejects them, so identity and the first phase-2 failure are deterministic?

quotes:
Lists
   whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by
   (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05,
   constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has
   the same identity; list values themselves keep their order.

constants, by (`to_node`, `to_port`): the port exists and is an input port
      of a node — never a flow output — of `value` carriage, the constant's
      declared schema is the port's stored schema (M21) — its value already
      fits that declared schema, composition refused it otherwise (rule 7), so
      it then fits the port;

fan-in, by (`to_node`, `to_port`): every input port of every node, and every
      flow output, has at least one source; a port with a constant has no other
      constant and no edge; and no two edges that can both deliver (rule 3) end at
      the same port, whatever its cardinality;
judgement.divergence: One implementer preserves submission order when constants have equal (`to_node`, `to_port`) keys, while another adds a value- or schema-based tie-breaker. The composing agent observes different `flow_version_id` values for reordered equal content and may observe a different constant named by the first phase-2 failure.
judgement.why: The declared ordering key does not totally order distinct constants targeting the same port, even though such constants reach identity computation and phase 2 before phase 6 rejects the duplicate.
judgement.deferred_to: the states whose texts it quotes

topics.topic: Deterministic ordering of FlowEdges with identical endpoints but different guards
questions: How are two edges with the same endpoints but different guards ordered, both for FlowVersion identity and for choosing the first proof failure?
How are two edges with identical endpoints but different guards ordered for identity hashing and first-failure selection?

quotes:
Lists
   whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by
   (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05,
   constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has
   the same identity; list values themselves keep their order.

edges, by (`to_node`, `to_port`, `from_node`, `from_port`): both ports exist
      with the right direction; both carry the same schema, the same carriage and,
      for files, the same media type (K-06) — cardinality is phase 5's; a flow
      input or output is `value` carriage;
judgement.divergence: One implementer preserves submission order for edges tied on all four endpoint fields, while another orders them by guard content. The composing agent observes different `flow_version_id` values after reordering the same edges and can receive a different edge as the first phase-3 or phase-4 proof failure.
judgement.why: The edge-order tuple omits the guard, so it does not totally order distinct edges with identical endpoints.
judgement.deferred_to: the states whose texts it quotes

topics.topic: HTTP protocol version and wire encoding or rejection of Unicode header values
questions: Which HTTP version is sent, may TLS negotiate HTTP/2, and how are accepted Unicode header values serialized or refused so that the described request and the request actually sent are the same?
How are non-ASCII required-header and credential values encoded on the HTTP wire, or are they invalid despite not being rejected by the stated checks?

judgement.why: HTTP protocol selection and wire encoding or rejection of header values are encoding and format contract questions assigned to State 6.

topics.topic: Required completeness and unexpected-name handling for authored trial ports
questions: Must inputs contain exactly every contract input and no extras, and when expected outputs are present must they contain exactly every contract output, or are partial expected outputs allowed?

Must authored trial inputs contain exactly every contract input and no extra names, and, when expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every contract output rather than a partial expected set? Also, where are unexpected names ordered among failures?

judgement.why: This is the same authored-trial map completeness and unexpected-name ordering question already decided by P10, and the relevant State 5 passages were not changed.

precedent.topic: Required completeness and handling of trial-case input and expected-output maps
quotes: add_trial_case: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises UnknownReferenceError for an unknown contract version; then RefusedError naming the first name in inputs that is not an input port of the contract version, then the first name in expected_outputs that is not an output port, each taken by name; then checks each input port and, when expected_outputs is given, each output port, in port name order, by fit_port_value with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant for value ports and the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant for file ports, a file candidate taking the payload's digest, size and the port's media type; the first failing check, presence, carriage, schema then size, raises RefusedError naming port and check, and nothing is written. A trial case therefore names exactly the contract's input ports, and expected_outputs is either absent or names exactly every output port: a partial expected_outputs, and an empty object, is given and fails presence at its first missing port; only absence means no expected outputs.
precedent.why: The later notes explicitly require exact input coverage and make expected outputs either absent or complete.

topics.topic: Timestamp semantics when an unknown EffectAttempt is later resolved
questions: When an `unknown` attempt is later resolved, does `concluded_at` retain the time it became unknown, change to the owner's resolution time, or is a separate resolution timestamp recorded?

When an EffectAttempt changes from unknown to applied or not_applied, is concluded_at preserved from the transport/recovery conclusion, overwritten with the owner's resolution time, or is a separate resolution timestamp required?

quotes: record_change: [BEHAVIOR] MUST apply the one StoreChange given in one SQLite transaction that either writes every record the variant lists or nothing; it writes no record the variant does not list and trusts the caller for every decision of the caller's rule, checking only its own invariants: attempt numbers, unique and existing identities, existing linked records, and no edit of an immutable record. Records of the kinds that are never edited — issued contract versions, implementations, trial cases, flow versions, values, verdicts, activations and trace records — are only ever written once; for any other entity a lifecycle change — a status, who decided, resolved, revoked, cancelled or released and when, concluded_at, ended_at, waiting points, outputs — updates those fields of the entity's one record in place, and the record keeps its store position, the position of its creation; no other field of a written record ever changes.

record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] RecordReadOutcomeChange writes the concluding NodeExecution with its StoredValues and SpooledFiles and no attempt; RecordOperationFailureChange writes one NodeExecution and no attempt; ResolveAttemptChange sets an unknown attempt to the = models.AttemptResolution value; GrantChange writes a StandingGrant with status active; RevokeChange sets an active grant to revoked with revoked_at; RecoverInFlightChange sets one in_flight attempt to unknown with concluded_at, writes its NodeExecution when given and sets used_approval_id's approval to used when given.

resolve_unknown_outcome: [BEHAVIOR] MUST write exactly one ResolveAttemptChange carrying the attempt key and the resolution, applied or not_applied, and return the EffectAttempt as written with resolved_by set; it writes no NodeExecution, so the attempt's one NodeExecution keeps outcome_unknown and the resolution is recorded nowhere else.
judgement.why: The later notes make resolution update only the attempt status and resolved_by, record no separate resolution fact, and prohibit changing any other field, so concluded_at is preserved.

What exact multipart serialization is used for boundary generation, CRLF placement, header formatting, quoting or escaping part names and filenames, and the closing delimiter?
